thread:
jamal_support: FYI customer AcmeHealth is getting a bunch of 429s during a traffic spike after they rotated their API key. They say headers show per-route remaining=0 but tenant overall quota not exhausted. Can we triage?

maria.sre: rough timeline + tenant id? do we have sample request_ids and model names?

jamal_support: tenant=acme-acmehealth, spike started ~16:03 UTC. Sample request log: 
```
{"ts":"2026-03-17T16:03:12Z","request_id":"req_9f2b","route":"/v1/generate","model":"redwood-2-small","status":429,"headers":{"X-RateLimit-Limit-route":"100","X-RateLimit-Remaining-route":"0","X-RateLimit-Reset-route":"16:03:40"}}
```
They also sent this curl repro they used: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <rotated-token>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-small","input":"hello","max_tokens":64}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```

alex.dev: tagging. Two quick hypotheses: (1) per-route quotas (beta) recently gate some routes and are enforced per model variant, or (2) route-to-model routing fallback sent them to a lower-capacity pool that has a smaller burst window.

kyle.eng-platform: we flipped the per_route_quota flag for a canary yesterday — checking deploys now. deploy-bot: per_route_quota flag enabled on canary at 2165439200, rollout stage=canary, owner=kyle.eng-platform.

maria.sre: ok that explains it if their requests went to canary nodes. jamal, can you pull a short sample trace around req_9f2b with headers + tenancy info? we need request_id, shard_id, model_variant and the rate-limit bucket id.

jamal_support: grabbed trace snippet from logs (sanitized): 
```
trace_id=req_9f2b shard=shard-12 model_variant=redwood-2-small pool=canary-burst bucket=tenant-route-100
headers: X-RateLimit-Bucket=tenant-route-100 X-RateLimit-Remaining=0
```

alex.dev: confirms per-route bucket name tenant-route-100 — sounds like a per-route-per-tenant bucket with limit 100. Platform level quota for tenant might be 10k/min but per-route was set lower for canary.

kyle.eng-platform: I can temporarily bump the canary per-route limit for tenant `acme-acmehealth` to reduce customer impact. but we should also add an alert / dashboard row for per-route bucket exhaustion. Where do you want the alert?

maria.sre: add to the rate-limits dashboard -> new panel: "per-route throttle rate (by tenant, route)" + rule: when rate_limit.count(bucket=*) > 0 for >2m AND pct_exhausted > 0.5 -> notify #eng-oncall + #support. Also add a quick Grafana link to prebuilt query.

jamal_support: customer asked for repro steps so they can test. alex, can you paste a repro command that hits the same per-route bucket?

alex.dev: use this internal diag curl to target the same bucket (don't share externally): 
```
for i in {1..150}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <their-token>" \
    -H "X-Debug-Bucket: tenant-route-100" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-2-small","input":"burst test"}' \
    https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
That will surface the 429s quickly. Recommend running from a bastion in the same region to mimic latency.

ashley-cs: I relayed to AcmeHealth. They are worried about billing anomalies — they saw a usage spike after rotation. Is there a way to correlate the spike to retry loops?

maria.sre: yes check request patterns for repeated request_ids or client-side retry headers. also look at token ingestion vs billed tokens: infra.lookup_billing(tenant=acme-acmehealth, start=2026-03-17T15:45Z, end=2026-03-17T16:20Z) -> shows token ingestion + retried_requests=462. If retried_requests high, that can cause billing + bursts.

jamal_support: customer says their SDK did an exponential backoff but with default max_retries=5. they rotated key and got a 401 for ~30s then retried which backfilled traffic all at once.

alex.dev: two action items: (A) short-term mitigation: kyle, bump per-route bucket limit for acme-acmehealth on canary to 1000 for 10m OR add a temporary routing rule to route them to dedicated pool. (B) longer-term: platform should ensure per-route quotas respect tenant-wide headroom and avoid canary-only tight buckets.

kyle.eng-platform: done — increased canary bucket limit for tenant acme-acmehealth to 1200 until 2165440150. also created alert `per_route_exhaustion_acme_acmehealth` in Grafana with eval window 2m.

deploy-bot: rollback suggestion: per_route_quota flag can be toggled on canary if we see broad impact. deploy-bot: latest canary config: per_route_quota=on, rollout=canary, affected_tenants=7.

maria.sre: please capture a playback of the spike for postmortem: snapshot telemetry for tenant-route-100 from 15:50-16:10 and include model variant breakdown + client_ip heatmap. jamal, please collect the customer-provided SDK logs and the server request_ids and attach to the case.

jamal_support: attaching logs to ticket now. customer wants confirmation the spike won't bill them for retries they didn't explicitly intend — can we put a billing credit hold while we investigate?

ashley-cs: I'll open a billing investigation and request temporary credit hold for acme-acmehealth. noted. :+1:

alex.dev: follow-up: we should add unit tests for per-route quota interactions with routing fallback and ensure simulated retries don't instantly exhaust per-route buckets. filing a small RFC to eng-platform.

kyle.eng-platform: I'll schedule a quick retro with platform + runtime + support tomorrow to tighten the observability around per-route buckets and ensure dashboard rows exist by default.

maria.sre: closing loop here — customer saw 429s stop after bump; no new occurrences in the last 6m. keeping the alert until 16:40 UTC. thanks team. :heart:
